recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-36030 unless a future work group decision defines repeated search result parameter behavior more precisely.
issue_request: FHIR-36030 was Published as Persuasive for R5. It asked how servers should handle repeated general/search result parameters such as _sort, _count, _summary, _elements, and _total; the accepted resolution clarified that, except for _include and _revInclude, search result parameters SHOULD only appear once, and repeated occurrences are undefined and may be treated as an error.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged commit a3a5c74c15013f3d02db070631edd347f7f8cf61 added the singleton guidance to source/search.html under Modifying Search Results. The later FHIR-22785 commit ebb31030e5595881bd9f0511dafcbdf6e26dac365 reorganized that section, added the result-parameter table, and preserved the guidance with code formatting and lower-case _revinclude.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2022-04-25 record the same clarification and a 10-0-0 vote. source/hierarchy.xml and source/documentation.html actively include search.html in the RESTful API/Search navigation, so source/search.html is in current build scope. Current source also says search result parameters are not SearchParameter resources and do not appear in the search parameter registry, keeping the rule scoped to result-control parameters. Targeted Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later conflicting FHIR-core decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because source/search.html:4982-4984 already contains the accepted conformance statement with both exceptions and the undefined/error behavior.
